name: Angkor Mandala Lab

scale.space: 18 x 12 synthetic patches (216 community agents), not spatially registered
scale.agents: 216 community patches (groups of households, population in thousands) and 5 court agents

claim_limits: Uncalibrated toy: outputs are implications of declared mechanisms, not estimates of Angkorian history.
No coefficient is fitted to any publication; the cited papers define benchmarks, not parameters.
Not modelled: warfare (the defense lever is inert), dynastic succession, temple estates, enslaved or corvee labour, fisheries, foreign polities, real GIS.
Decline-event frequencies are frequencies across simulated worlds under fixed assumptions, not probabilities of historical events.
theory_sources: Wolters / Southeast Asian mandala: allegiance to overlapping centres
Menefee: Rice Domus and Networked Domus (worlds/angkor/context/)

mechanisms.statement: Communities pledge each decade to the court with the best score: log prestige minus transport cost (scaled by local autonomy) plus fertility plus noise.
mechanisms.note: Mandala model of overlapping, shifting allegiance.

mechanisms.statement: Movement by water costs half as much as overland (boat discount on Euclidean distance).
mechanisms.note: Not a least-cost network; no seasonality.

mechanisms.statement: Engineered water raises output and productive capacity; extreme wet years damage it; maintenance spending repairs it.
mechanisms.ablation: no_water removes BOTH the gain and the damage (compound ablation)
mechanisms.note: Penny et al. 2018 (climate-driven cascading failure) vs Penny et al. 2019 (decline first, infrastructure neglected after).

mechanisms.statement: Tax reach falls with distance to the pledged court: exp(-cost/8), reduced by local autonomy.
Court prestige follows resources: sqrt of aligned population and of revenue, with persistence 0.85.
mechanisms.note: Ritual, dynastic and military sources of prestige are not represented.

mechanisms.statement: Maritime trade opportunity rises on a logistic curve centred on 1200 CE.
mechanisms.note: CALENDAR-ANCHORED exogenous forcing (centre 1200, scale 85 years). Not a scripted collapse, but a dated input.

mechanisms.statement: Rainfall = deterministic cycle sin((year-710)/31) (period about 195 years) + stochastic shocks + occasional extremes.
mechanisms.note: CALENDAR-ANCHORED climate cycle; uncalibrated. The random stream depends on shock_intensity (draws are conditional), so high_shock does not share realised weather with reference.

mechanisms.statement: Population grows toward a carrying capacity set by fertility, managed water and soil; drought and stress raise mortality.
Communities move up to 4% of population per decade to the richest neighbouring patch (exit).
mechanisms.note: Scott: exit; no movement off the board.

mechanisms.statement: Soil is exhausted by irrigation under stress and restored by community labour (local autonomy).
The defense lever and court treasuries are computed but affect nothing else.
mechanisms.note: Audit finding: present in outputs, absent from causation.

struts.statement: A grid cell represents a community of households; populations are in thousands.
Fertility, waterway route and polity locations are stylized, not a GIS reconstruction.
Output, tax, maintenance and migration coefficients are illustrative, unfitted.
A maritime-market trend is an external opportunity, not an algorithmic decline trigger.
One decade per tick; rain shocks are stochastic; temperature/rain proxies uncalibrated.
Allegiance is recomputed from prestige, distance and coercive capacity, not dynastic events.
State courts are candidate sites: Angkor, West, East, South, Highlands.
Court institutions/rituals are reduced to prestige; military rivalry to contestation.
Agricultural land has an illustrative carrying capacity and depends on maintenance.
Trade at boundary is exogenous; no explicit Champa, Dai Viet, or Chinese agents.
Initial prestige: Angkor 1.09, West 0.79, East 0.77, South port 0.68, Upland 0.60.
Court sites on the grid: Angkor (8,6), West (3,7), East (15,6), South port (12,10), Upland (8,2).
struts.provenance: illustrative assumption; not registered to real geography

interventions._note: Bounds are proposed ranges for experiments, not evidence-based. Interventions are landscape-wide regimes: courts do not choose them (audit finding).

benchmarks.name: Angkor is the leading centre c. 1200
benchmarks.observable: strongest court by aligned population in 1200 == Angkor
benchmarks.source: General historiography: Angkor as capital of the Khmer polity from the late 9th century; height under Jayavarman VII (r. c. 1181-1218). E.g. Higham, The Civilization of Angkor (2001).
benchmarks.note: The model mapping (leading in aligned population on a synthetic board) is itself an interpretive choice.

benchmarks.name: Peak population of Greater Angkor about 700,000-900,000
benchmarks.source: Klassen et al. 2021, Science Advances, "Diachronic modeling of the population within the medieval Greater Angkor Region settlement complex": approximately 700,000 to 900,000 inhabitants at its apogee in the 13th century CE. https://scholarsbank.uoregon.edu/items/4531bb7d-727f-4115-a844-1c320edbeea7/full
benchmarks.note: Diagnostic only: the synthetic board has no spatial registration, so its total is not the Greater Angkor Region. Becomes a test after spatial registration (plan step 1).

benchmarks.name: Apogee in the 13th century
benchmarks.observable: year of peak Angkor-aligned population in 1200-1299

benchmarks.name: Gradual decline from the early 1300s, not abrupt collapse
benchmarks.observable: Angkor-aligned population lower in 1450 than in 1300, and no decade-to-decade fall above 15% in 1300-1450
benchmarks.source: Penny et al. 2019, PNAS: land use in the urban core declined from the early 1300s; the Angkor Thom moat was unmaintained by the late 14th century; gradual decline rather than collapse in 1431. https://sciencedaily.com/releases/2019/02/190225192144.htm
benchmarks.note: Rival reading to B5 on what came first.

benchmarks.name: Water network degrades after a mid-14th-century drought-to-wet shift
benchmarks.observable: mean water condition in 1350-1450 below its 1200-1300 mean
benchmarks.source: Penny et al. 2018, Science Advances: cascading failure of an overloaded canal network under a mid-14th-century shift from prolonged drought to very wet years. https://sciencedaily.com/releases/2018/10/181018095435.htm
benchmarks.note: Passing B5 shows the model can produce degradation, not that the climate story is right; B4 vs B5 is the ordering question.
